findings.claim: a symlinked folder selected no files, so run --delete wiped the prefix
no CLI-level assertion that ovsq run exits 1 on a failed upload
docs said Prepare errors exit differently than they do
the final manifest write used the cancelled context
the main.go usage text's exit-status paragraph does not list the refused --delete as an exit-1 case, unlike the reference page and README

verdict.text: All four findings are fixed, and the fixes break nothing.
The symlinked-folder delete bug is closed twice: the scan now resolves the root, and a guard refuses `--delete` when the scan selected nothing but the manifest still lists files.
One small new docs gap is left (f5): the CLI usage text does not mention the refused `--delete`.
It does not block.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: `stamp green: 5136f734bac7ba8fb97608c5bfc9f54ab08e2677b0d851d77b12245b4bfdae24`.
lint, format and rows r1-r9 and r11 pass.
`bash packages/ov-sync-queue/check.sh`: all packages pass.
scan.Select: EvalSymlinks then Stat+IsDir, and the error names the original path.
Engine.Root keeps the unresolved path, and that is fine: Hash and ReadFile follow the link, and Rel comes from the resolved root.
Include folders are still Lstat'ed under the resolved root, so their escape check is unchanged.
syncer.Run guard: `del && len(p.selected)==0 && len(p.Deletes)>0`.
p.selected also counts skipped and unreadable files, so a folder that holds only oversized files does not trip it.
The guard adds a failure, so the run exits 1, and it sets del=false, so the summary reports 0 to delete and nothing is removed from the manifest.
Uploads cannot happen when nothing is selected, so this path writes no manifest.
TestDeleteSafety, symlink subtest: it needs exit 0 and zero writes through the link.
The guard alone would exit 1 and fail it, so the test really covers the scan fix.
Refusal subtest: it checks exit 1, the "refusing" text and no DELETE.
TestSelection now has subtests for a symlinked root and for a root that is a file or missing.
TestRunFailuresKeepManifestTrue (main_test.go) checks exit 1 and the old hash kept.
Row r4's `./...` regex runs it next to the syncer test with the same name.
TestManifestWriteSurvivesCancel: cancelStore makes the manifest Put fail on a cancelled ctx, so without WithoutCancel the test would fail.
Both the checkpoint and final writes use keepCtx.
Uploads and deletes still respect cancellation.
The docs reference page's exit-code table and the README now match the code paths (main.go returns 1 at the Prepare and run failures, 2 for usage and config errors).
f1 resolved: scan.go:37-44 resolves and checks the root, and syncer.go:214-220 adds the refusal guard.
Tests: TestSelection symlink and bad-root subtests, and both TestDeleteSafety subtests.
f2 resolved: main_test.go:305 asserts exit 1 from `ovsq run` and that the manifest entry is kept.
f3 resolved: the reference page's exit-code table and the usage text cover unreadable folder, include folder, git and manifest as exit 1.
f4 resolved: syncer.go:189 uses context.WithoutCancel for both manifest writes, tested by TestManifestWriteSurvivesCancel.
f5 open (docs, non-blocking): the usage text at main.go:40-42 lists the exit-1 causes but leaves out the `--delete` refused because nothing was selected.
The implementer's brief says it covers it.
Add "or --delete was refused because no files were selected".
